belongs_to: 'Visualising the problem as shown, we have to find out how many 20 cm make 3,84,400 km.' (Linear Growth vs. Exponential Growth; the ladder from the Earth to the Moon)
description: Black hand-drawn line sketch, no colour, 16:9-ish wide strip, labels in handwriting. LEFT: a large circle labelled 'Earth' (label above the circle's top-left). RIGHT: a smaller circle labelled 'Moon' (label above the circle); the Earth circle is clearly larger than the Moon circle. LADDER drawn flat, lying horizontally between them: two long parallel horizontal rails starting at the right edge of the Earth circle and running right for about 40% of the gap (the top rail ends a little before the bottom rail); 6 vertical rungs join the rails (the first rung touches the Earth circle), so 5 boxes are visible between rungs. After the last rung the ladder is continued only by a row of small dots at mid-height of the ladder (about 15 dots, hand-drawn) that runs on towards the Moon and stops short of the Moon circle. MEASUREMENTS: (a) two short dashed vertical lines drop down from the bottom rail at the 2nd and 3rd rungs; between them a short double-headed horizontal arrow with the label '20 cm' written above the arrow, so one step (gap between consecutive rungs) = 20 cm; (b) the dashed lines continue down to a long double-headed horizontal arrow that starts at the left end of the ladder (at the Earth's edge) and ends below the left part of the Moon circle; the label '3,84,400 km' is written under the middle of this long arrow. Nothing else is drawn (no stars, no people).
unclear: Rung count read as 6 vertical lines / 5 boxes (hand-drawn, unevenly spaced); the dotted continuation has about 15 dots and could be 15 to 17.
Right end of the long 3,84,400 km arrow stops under the left half of the Moon circle, not exactly at its centre.

belongs_to: 'Linear growth is additive, whereas exponential growth is multiplicative.' (the two expressions with braces under 'To cover the distance between the Earth and the Moon, it takes 1,92,20,00,000 steps with linear growth whereas it takes just 46 folds of a piece of paper with exponential growth!')
description: Two printed expressions side by side, each with a curly brace (opening downward) drawn under it and a label under the brace's point; no colour. LEFT: the text '20 + 20 + 20 + …………' (three 20s joined by + signs followed by a row of dots); a curly brace under the whole expression; label under the brace's tip on two lines: '1,92,20,00,000' and 'times'. RIGHT: the text '0.001 × 2 × 2 × 2 ……….' (0.001 then three 2s joined by × signs and a row of dots); a curly brace under it that starts under the first '2' (the brace does not cover the 0.001) and runs to the right end of the dots; label under the brace's tip: '46 times'. The left expression is the linear (additive) growth, the right one the exponential (multiplicative) growth.

belongs_to: 'Getting a Sense for Large Numbers' - list of facts for 10^10 to 10^25 (continued); the mosquito entry has a blank; the 'Calculate and write the answer using scientific notation' questions (i) ants per human, (ii) flocks of starlings, (iii) leaves on all trees, (iv) sheets of paper to the Moon work on these numbers
description: Two-column hanging-indent list continued (power in the left margin column; fact text on the right; no rules, no colour). Before it, the boxed-question line: 'With a global human population of about 8 × 10^9 and about 4 × 10^5 African elephants, can we say that there are nearly 20,000 people for every African elephant?'. 8 entries in this order: 10^10: global chicken population living at any time ≈ 33 billion (3.3 × 10^10). 10^12: estimated number of trees (2023) globally 30 kharab / 3 trillion (3 × 10^12); one kharab is 100 arab, one trillion is 1000 billion. 10^14: estimated mosquito population worldwide (2023) 11 neel / 110 trillion (a BLANK bracket '( ________ )' for the student); derived estimate of the Antarctic krill population 50 neel / 500 trillion (5 × 10^14). 10^15: beetle population estimate 1 padma / 1 quadrillion (1 × 10^15); earthworm population also 1 padma / 1 quadrillion. 10^16: estimated ant population 20 padma / 20 quadrillion (2 × 10^16); 'Ants alone outweigh all wild birds and wild mammals combined.' 10^21 (this entry is a normal full-width paragraph, the '10^21' is the first word, not in the margin): supposed number of grains of sand on all beaches and deserts on Earth; 'enough sand to give every ant 10 little sand castles to live in.' 10^23: estimated number of stars in the observable universe is 2 × 10^23. 10^25: an estimated 2 × 10^25 drops of water on Earth (assuming 16 drops per millilitre). Illustrations beside/inside it (decorative, not listed separately): a krill picture, the balance picture (listed as P20-balance-1) and a wide picture of sand castles with one small ant at the right end.
unclear: Sand-castle and krill illustrations are decorative and not listed separately.

belongs_to: Illustration beside the entry '10^16 ... Ants alone outweigh all wild birds and wild mammals combined.'
description: Colour illustration of a two-pan balance (weighing scale), no numbers or labels. The beam is tilted: its left end is low, its right end high. LEFT pan (small round dish hanging from the beam by three strings) holds a black heap of ants. RIGHT pan (a dark boat-shaped tray hanging from the right end of the beam on two rods) is crowded with wild animals and birds (an elephant, giraffe, gorilla, deer, lion, tiger, monkey, peacock and other birds). The left (ants) pan hangs lower than the right (animals) pan, i.e. the ants side is the heavier. A thin horizontal line and a vertical line frame the upper right of the scale as part of the stand.
unclear: Purely pictorial comparison (qualitative, no numbers); may be judged decorative later. Individual animals were not counted.

belongs_to: 'We shall look at approximate times and timelines of some events and phenomena, and use powers of 10 to represent and compare these quantities.' - table 'Time in seconds | Comparison to real-world events/phenomena', first part (10^0, 10^1, 10^2)
description: Two-column table, first part. Header: a pink band across the full width with the bold titles 'Time in seconds' (left column) and 'Comparison to real-world events/phenomena' (right column), a thin dark rule under the header. Body rows have no ruled lines and no colour; the right column items start with a '-' dash. Rows on this page: (1) '10^0 = 1 second' | '- Time taken for a ball thrown up to fall back on the ground (typically a few seconds).' (2) '10^1 = 10 seconds' | '- Time blood takes to complete one full circulation through the body: 10–20 seconds (1 × 10^1 – 2 × 10^1 seconds).' and '- Typical waiting time at a traffic signal.' Rows 1 and 2 give '= 1 second' / '= 10 seconds'; row 3 gives only '≈1.6 minutes'. 3 rows, 5 bulleted comparisons on this page. The table continues on p.22 without a repeated header.
unclear: The 10^2 row continues the same table after the owl box (it has no header or rule of its own).

belongs_to: Continuation of the table 'Time in seconds | Comparison to real-world events/phenomena' (10^3, 10^4, then 10^7, 10^8, 10^9); between 10^4 and 10^7 a boxed question asks for events of the order of 10^5 and 10^6 seconds
description: Two-column table continued (no header band repeated, no ruled lines, no colour, dash bullets in the right column), 5 rows: (1) '10^3 seconds ≈ 16.6 minutes' | '- Satellites in low Earth orbits take between 90 minutes (≈ 5.5 × 10^3 seconds) to 2 hours to complete one full revolution around the Earth.' (2) '10^4 seconds ≈ 2.7 hours' | '- The time needed to digest a meal: about 2–4 hours to pass through the stomach.' and '- Lifespan of an adult mayfly: about a day (≈ 9 × 10^4 seconds).' [mayfly illustration at the right]. Then the printed question breaks the table (rows 10^5 and 10^6 are NOT in the table): '10^5 seconds ≈ 1.16 days and 10^6 seconds ≈ 11.57 days. Think of some events or phenomena whose time is of the order of (i) 10^5 seconds and (ii) 10^6 seconds. Write them in scientific notation.' (3) '10^7 seconds ≈ 115.7 days / ≈ 3.8 months' | '- Time spent sleeping in a year: about 4 months.', '- Time taken by Mangalyaan mission to reach Mars: 298 days (≈ 2.65 × 10^7 seconds).', '- Time taken by Mars for one full revolution around the Sun: 687 Earth-days/1.88 Earth-years (≈ 6 × 10^7 seconds).' [Mangalyaan picture at the right] (4) '10^8 seconds ≈ 3.17 years' | '- The typical lifespan of most dogs is 3 to 15 years.' (5) '10^9 seconds ≈ 31.7 years' | '- The orbital period of Halley's comet is 75–79 years; the next expected return is in the year 2061 (≈ 2.4 × 10^9 seconds).' and '- Duration of one full revolution of Neptune around the Sun: 60,190 Earth-days/~165 Earth-years or 89,666 Neptunian days/1 Neptunian-year (≈ 5.2 × 10^9 seconds). A day on Neptune is about 16.1 hours'. 5 rows, 9 bulleted comparisons. At the top of the page a 3-panel comic (Roxie with a noodle packet 'These liars!! It never gets cooked before 10 minutes...', Estu 'They should approximate it as order of 10^2 seconds noodles - that way whether it takes 120 seconds or 900 seconds, the claim will be true.', both laughing) - dialogue picture, decorative.

belongs_to: Continuation of the table 'Time in seconds | Comparison to real-world events/phenomena' (10^10 to 10^15); the Kelenken row has a blank for the student

belongs_to: 'The modern naming is similar to this, where we say,' - Indian naming: hundred thousand = lakh, hundred lakhs = crore, hundred crores = arab, hundred arab = kharab (section 2.5 'A Pinch of History')
description: Three-column table with no ruled lines and no colour, centred text, 4 rows (no header row). Column 1 (words, two lines each) | column 2 (numerals) | column 3 (powers of 10): (1) 'A hundred thousand is a lakh' | '100 × 1000 = 1,00,000' | '10^2 × 10^3 = 10^5'. (2) 'A hundred lakhs is a crore' | '100 × 1,00,000 = 1,00,00,000' | '10^2 × 10^5 = 10^7'. (3) 'A hundred crores is an arab' | '100 × 1,00,00,000 = 1,00,00,00,000' | '10^2 × 10^7 = 10^9'. (4) 'A hundred arab is a kharab' | '100 × 1,00,00,00,000' on one line and '= 1,00,00,00,00,000' on a second line | '10^2 × 10^9 = 10^11'. Text after the table: a hundred kharab is a neel (10^13), a hundred neel a padma (10^15), a hundred padma a shankh (10^17), a hundred shankh a maha shankh (10^19).

unclear: The trillion value is printed '1,00,000,000,000' (Indian-style commas) in the International table - read as printed.
